proposals.entity_key: Other negations (personne, jamais, plus, rien, guère)
value: ne is required before the verb in standard written French
personne, rien, and jamais can also function as subjects (Personne ne vient), in which case they precede ne
guère is restricted to formal or literary French

evidence.notes: Built from the rule's construction and the trap noting guère is formal; subject use of personne/rien/jamais is standard usage.

value: Only when the antecedent expresses a place
Cannot be preceded by a preposition; à où and de où do not occur

evidence.notes: First entry from the stated condition; the preposition restriction is standard grammar with medium confidence.

value: Only when the antecedent expresses time (e.g. l'année, le jour, l'instant, le siècle)
Où here means 'when' and does not replace a place prepositional phrase

evidence.notes: Derived from the stated condition and the examples given in the rule.

proposals.entity_key: Partitive article: du, de la, de l', des
value: Limited to mass nouns and plural count nouns whose quantity is unspecified
Becomes de (or d' before a vowel) in negative sentences, except after être
Not used after quantity expressions, which take de alone (beaucoup de, trop de)

evidence.notes: First two entries come from the rule's conditions and negative_form; the quantity-expression limit is standard usage.

value: Limited to pronominal verbs such as se dire, se traduire, se voir, se boire
No agent is expressed with this passive meaning

evidence.notes: Based on the listed related verbs and the passive meaning described; medium confidence on the exact verb set.

proposals.entity_key: Passive used to avoid specifying agent
value: Used only when the agent is unknown, unimportant, or deliberately omitted
If the agent must be named, the active voice or an explicit par-phrase is used instead

evidence.notes: Follows from the stated usage; the alternative construction is standard usage.

value: Used only when the receiver of the action is the focus of the sentence
Not used when the agent is the more important element of the message

evidence.notes: Derived from the stated emphasis on the subject and the contrast with agent focus.

value: Limited to transitive verbs that can take a direct object
The past participle agrees with the subject, not with the agent
Never formed with avoir as the auxiliary

evidence.notes: Second entry is stated in the rule; the transitivity and avoir restrictions are standard grammar with medium confidence.

value: Requires an auxiliary (avoir or être); a single conjugated verb is not a passé composé
Most verbs take avoir, while a limited set of verbs and all pronominal verbs take être
Only the auxiliary is negated, with ne...pas surrounding it

evidence.notes: First two entries follow from the formation; the negation placement matches the rule's negative_form.

proposals.entity_key: Past conditional for regret or reproach
value: Limited to unrealized past actions, not to present or future ones
Typically used with verbs such as devoir, pouvoir, vouloir, and aimer plus an infinitive

evidence.notes: Based on the usage notes and the related expressions/verbs listed for the rule.
